title: The path to Brahman (18.49–18.58)
hook: near the end, Krishna draws the whole road in ten verses
tomorrow: "I have told you. Now do as you choose." (18.59–18.66)

segments.voice: Yesterday, svadharma: your own dharma, even imperfect, and every fire has some smoke. Today, where that road leads.

Near the end of a long hike, someone who's walked it before often stops the group at a clearing and points. See that ridge? We came over that. See the river? We crossed it. And there, the summit. That's where we're going. It doesn't make the last stretch shorter, but suddenly the whole trail makes sense. Chapter eighteen has a passage like that. In about ten verses, Krishna draws the whole road, from ordinary work all the way to Brahman, and to love beyond it.
screen: `A CLEARING NEAR THE END.` → `THE RIDGE, THE RIVER.` → `AND THERE, THE SUMMIT.`

segments.voice: Verse forty-nine: with understanding unattached everywhere, self mastered, desire gone, a person reaches through relinquishment the highest perfection, freedom from the bind of action. Verse fifty: now hear, briefly, how the one who's reached that perfection reaches Brahman. Then the road, verses fifty-one to fifty-three. A clear understanding. Holding yourself steady with resolve. Setting aside sound and the other sense objects, putting down liking and disliking. Seeking quiet, solitary places, eating lightly, speech, body and mind held in check. Always turning to meditation, resting in dispassion. Letting go of ego, force, pride, desire, anger, and the need to own things. Free of mine, at peace. That one, Krishna says, is fit to become Brahman. The word that holds it together is dhriti, steadiness, resolve. Not a burst of effort. A steady hand. Then verse fifty-four, the summit, and a surprise. Having become Brahman, serene, that person neither grieves nor craves. The same toward all beings, they reach the highest love for me. One might expect the road to end in a merging where love disappears. Here, on becoming Brahman, love begins. Verse fifty-five: by love they know me as I truly am, and knowing me, they enter me. Advaita teachers read this as knowledge completing itself; Vaishnava teachers read it as devotion as the goal. Both keep the verse. Then Krishna turns to Arjuna. Verse fifty-seven: give all your actions to me in your mind. Verse fifty-eight: with your mind on me, by my grace you'll cross every obstacle. But if, out of ego, you won't listen, you'll be lost.
screen: `PERFECTION THROUGH LETTING GO.` · `STEADY: SIMPLE, QUIET, FREE OF MINE.` · `BECOMING BRAHMAN, LOVE BEGINS.` · `BY MY GRACE YOU'LL CROSS.` · then, large: `THE PATH TO BRAHMAN.`

segments.voice: Try one piece of the road, steadiness: spine upright, breath even. When a sound comes, let it pass without liking or disliking it; when a thought of mine comes, my plans, my things, let it pass too. Don't force anything; just hold steady, like a hand around a cup of water, firm but not tight.
Brahmabhuta, having become Brahman. Gita eighteen, forty-nine to fifty-eight: relinquishment, steadiness, a quiet, solitary life free of mine, becoming Brahman, and then the highest love.
Your line: steady. From the clearing, the summit and the whole road are in view. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Hindu teachers read Gita 18.49–18.58 as a summary of the whole spiritual path, from unattached work and disciplined living to realizing Brahman and supreme devotion (para bhakti).
